Let $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$ with $a < b$ and let $f : [a,b] \to \mathbb{R}$ be continuous on $[a,b]$ ([[def-continuity-real]], [[def-interval]]) and differentiable at every point of $(a,b)$ as a function on $[a,b]$ ([[def-derivative]]). Then there is $c \in (a,b)$ with $$f(b) - f(a) \;=\; f'(c)\,(b - a) .$$

This item fixes the **scattering data** of the restricted model class of
[[post-cm05-central-model]] and the preparation conventions in which the
scattering statements of this page are phrased. All objects are model data;
nothing here is a measured value.

**(i) The scattering model.** A **central scattering model** is a model of
class (i) of [[post-cm05-central-model]] with $N=2$ labels, masses
$m_1,m_2>0$ ([[post-cm01-worldlines]] clause (v)), no external forces, and a
static central pair potential $u\in C^2(J_0)$
([[def-cm-scattering-data]], [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]])
whose collision-excluded interval satisfies $(0,\infty)\subseteq J_0$, so
that the only forbidden configuration is the collision $r=0$. Its **reduced
problem** is the one-label problem of class (ii) with reduced mass
$\mu:=m_1m_2/(m_1+m_2)$ ([[def-cm01-units]]: $[\mu]=\mathsf M$) and the same
potential, presented through the relative coordinate $r=x_1-x_2$; by
[[pthm-cm05-relative-reduction]] the relative coordinate of every motion of
the model is a central-force trajectory for $(\mu,u)$ and every pair of an
affine centre-of-mass motion and a solution of the reduced equation on a
common interval reconstructs a motion of the model.

**(ii) Scattering motions and their data.** Let $r:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^3$
be a central-force trajectory for $(\mu,u)$ defined on all of $\mathbb R$
with values $|r(t)|\in J_0$ and with constant angular momentum
$j=\mu\,r\times r'=Je_3\ne0$ for $J>0$ and an oriented orthonormal triad
$(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ ([[def-cm-central-force-trajectory]],
[[thm-cm-central-force-angular-momentum-conservation]],
[[thm-cm-central-force-polar-reduction]],
[[lem-cm-oriented-orthonormal-triads]]). Call $r$ a **scattering motion** of
the model when it satisfies the hypotheses under which the page's scattering
theorems establish the limits below. Its **energy** is the constant
$$E:=\tfrac12\mu\lVert r'\rVert_2^2+u(\lvert r\rvert)>0$$
of [[def-cm-central-force-trajectory]] (constant by
[[thm-cm-central-force-polar-reduction]] clause 4), its **asymptotic
velocities** are the limits
$$v_-:=\lim_{t\to-\infty}r'(t),\qquad v_+:=\lim_{t\to+\infty}r'(t),$$
taken in the sense of [[def-vector-valued-functions-limits-and-continuity]]
(their existence under the hypotheses is a theorem, not a convention), and
its **scattering speed** is
$$v_\infty:=\lVert v_-\rVert_2=\lVert v_+\rVert_2=\sqrt{2E/\mu},$$
the equality being part of the scattering theorems. The **incoming branch**
is the trajectory restricted to times before its apsis; the **impact
parameter** is the perpendicular distance from the force centre of the line
through the incoming branch, defined by
$$b:=\frac{\lVert r(t)\times v_-\rVert_2}{\lVert v_-\rVert_2} \qquad(t\ \text{on the incoming branch}),$$
with $\times$ the cross product of [[def-cross-product-in-r3]] and the
Euclidean norm of [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]; the value is independent
of $t$ because $r\times r'=j/\mu$ is constant, and the scattering theorems
identify it with the geometric distance, giving $b=J/(\mu v_\infty)$. Its
dimension is $[b]=\ell$.

**(iii) Polar advance and deflection conventions.** Fix polar data
$(\rho,\theta)$ of the scattering motion in the triad, $r=\rho\,n(\theta)$,
$n(\varphi):=\cos\varphi\,e_1+\sin\varphi\,e_2$
([[thm-cm-central-force-polar-reduction]]), and let $t_*$ be an apsis time,
$|r(t_*)|=\min_t|r(t)|$. The **polar advance of one half** is
$$\Delta:=\theta(+\infty)-\theta(t_*)=\theta(t_*)-\theta(-\infty),$$
defined by the limits asserted in the scattering theorems, and the
**polar advance of the motion** is $2\Delta$. The **scattering angle** is the
undirected angle between the asymptotic velocity directions,
$$\theta_{\mathrm{s}}:=\arccos\!\left(\frac{\langle v_-,v_+\rangle}{\lVert v_-\rVert_2\,\lVert v_+\rVert_2}\right)\in[0,\pi],$$
equivalently the angle between the incoming and outgoing asymptote lines;
the **signed velocity rotation** is the continuous rotation angle of
$r'(t)$, measured counterclockwise about $e_3$ relative to the incoming
direction, so that a positive value is a counterclockwise turn. The scattering
theorems give $\cos\theta_{\mathrm{s}}=\cos(\pi-2\Delta)$ and the signed
rotation $2\Delta-\pi$; in particular, when $0<\Delta<\pi/2$ the scattering
angle is
$$\theta_{\mathrm{s}}=\pi-2\Delta\in(0,\pi),$$
while for $\Delta\ge\pi/2$ the motion has wrapped past the backward direction
and $\theta_{\mathrm{s}}$ is the wrapped value $\arccos(\cos(\pi-2\Delta))$.
The **deflection map** of a scattering model is the partial map
$b\mapsto\theta_{\mathrm{s}}(b)$ carrying the impact parameter of each
scattering motion that satisfies the hypotheses to its scattering angle;
the scattering theorems of the page determine its values on the hypotheses
they state, and **deflection branches** of it are the $C^1$ branches of
[[def-cm-scattering-data]].

**(iv) The uniform-incident preparation (adopted model datum).** The
**uniform-incident preparation** of a central scattering model with cutoff
$b_{\max}>0$ and flux $\Phi>0$ is the following adopted model of a scattering
experiment for the reduced problem: independent incident reduced labels, each
with energy $E>0$, angular momentum $Je_3$ and impact-azimuth pair
distributed with density $b\,\mathrm db\,\mathrm d\varphi$ on
$(0,b_{\max})\times(0,2\pi)$ normalised to unit total mass, where the
**incident flux** $\Phi$ is the number of incident labels per unit area per
unit time and $[\Phi]=\ell^{-2}\tau^{-1}$ ([[def-cm01-units]]). Under this
preparation the model predicts the expected rate
$$\dot N(A)= \Phi\cdot\nu(A)$$
of incident labels whose impact-azimuth pair lies in $A$, where $\nu$ is the
incident flux measure of [[def-cm-scattering-data]]; the rate of scattered
labels into a solid-angle set is the flux times the pushforward of $\nu$ under
the deflection map, whose density on a branch is the cross-section density
introduced in this page's cross-section definition. This is a predicted model
quantity: it reports no
detection, and its comparison with data requires a separately specified
experiment, apparatus model and statistical analysis.

**(v) Reading conventions.** All angles and lengths above are data of the
**relative** problem, equivalently of the centre-of-mass frame of the
two-label model: the relative coordinate $r$ and the centre of mass $X$ are
those of clause (i) and [[def-cm03-centre-of-mass-and-momenta]]. The
individual labels move along $x_1=X+\frac{m_2}{M}r$ and
$x_2=X-\frac{m_1}{M}r$ with $M=m_1+m_2$
([[pthm-cm05-relative-reduction]] clause 4), so their directions relative to
the centre of mass differ from $r$ by the mass factors and generally differ
from each other; an angle of the reduced problem is not, without further
computation, an angle of either label with respect to a laboratory frame.
"Target", "projectile" and "detector" are names for model components and
carry no empirical claim.

**(vi) Exclusions and status.** The class excludes velocity- or
time-dependent, non-central and non-potential forces; constraints and
reaction forces; collisions $r=0$; external forces; and models with more than
two labels, exactly as in [[post-cm05-central-model]] clause (v). The
preparation of clause (iv) is one adopted idealisation among many; the
scattering theorems state separately which potentials, energies and angular
momenta produce the data of clauses (ii)-(iii). The quantities $\mu$, $u$
(with any parameters it carries), $E$, $J$, $b$, $b_{\max}$, $\Phi$ are model
data; quantitative empirical use requires separately stated measured inputs
with uncertainties, and no statement of this page asserts that any physical
system is exactly a central scattering model or that any beam is exactly
uniform.

**Why the objects are defined.** The relative coordinate is a central-force
trajectory by the cited reduction theorem; the attached energy and angular
momentum are defined by [[def-cm-central-force-trajectory]] and are constant
on the trajectory by [[thm-cm-central-force-polar-reduction]] clause 4 and
[[thm-cm-central-force-angular-momentum-conservation]]; the impact parameter
is $t$-independent because $r\times r'=j/\mu$ is constant; and the
preparation measure of clause (iv) is the measure $\nu$ of
[[def-cm-scattering-data]]. The arccosine of clause (iii) is defined because
the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality gives
$|\langle v_-,v_+\rangle|/(\lVert v_-\rVert_2\lVert v_+\rVert_2)\le1$
([[def-euclidean-inner-product]]).

**Mathematical status.** The vocabulary is attached to the adopted model
class of [[post-cm05-central-model]]; the existence of the limits, the
identities for $v_\infty$, $b$, $\Delta$ and $\theta_{\mathrm{s}}$, and the
form of the deflection map under explicit potential hypotheses are the
content of the mathematics and physics theorems of this page, not of this
definition.

Adopt a central scattering model of [[def-cm15-asymptotic-data]] clause (i)
with masses $m_1,m_2>0$, reduced mass $\mu=m_1m_2/(m_1+m_2)$, static
central pair potential $u\in C^2((0,\infty))$
([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]), and let $E>0$, $J>0$; write
$$V(r):=u(r)+\frac{J^2}{2\mu r^2}\qquad(r>0).$$
Suppose:

**(H1) finite range:** there is $R>0$ with $u(r)=0$ for every $r\ge R$;

**(H2) simple outer turning point:** there is $r_*>0$ with
$$V(r_*)=E,\qquad V'(r_*)<0,\qquad V(r)<E\quad(r>r_*).$$

Let $r:J_0\to\mathbb R^3$ be the relative coordinate of a motion of the model
on an interval $J_0$ with nonempty interior and with attached angular
momentum $j=\mu\,r\times r'=Je_3\ne0$ and attached energy $E$
([[def-cm-central-force-trajectory]],
[[pthm-cm05-relative-reduction]]), and suppose
$|r(t)|\ge r_*$ for every $t\in J_0$ and $|r(t_*)|=r_*$ for some
$t_*\in J_0$. Then:

1. **(The scattering motion.)** $r$ extends uniquely to a central-force
   trajectory $\bar r:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^3$ for $(\mu,u)$; the extension is
   the relative coordinate of a motion of the two-label model defined on all
   of $\mathbb R$, whose centre of mass is the affine extension of the
   original one. Along $\bar r$, $\rho:=|\bar r|$ satisfies $\rho\ge r_*$,
   $\rho(t)>r_*$ for $t\ne t_*$, and $\rho$ is strictly decreasing on
   $(-\infty,t_*]$ and strictly increasing on $[t_*,\infty)$; no collision
   occurs. Moreover the time quadrature
   $$\tau(r_0):=\int_{r_*}^{r_0}\frac{\mathrm ds}{\sqrt{(2/\mu)\bigl(E-V(s)\bigr)}}\qquad(r_0\ge r_*)$$
   is finite for every $r_0$ and satisfies $\rho(t_*\pm\tau(r_0))=r_0$.
2. **(Free asymptotes, speed and impact parameter.)** The limits
   $v_\pm=\lim_{t\to\pm\infty}\bar r'(t)$ exist and
   $$|v_+|=|v_-|=\sqrt{2E/\mu}=:v_\infty .$$
   For every $t_1\ge t_*$ with $\rho(t_1)\ge R$ the motion is exactly free
   from $t_1$ on, $\bar r(t)=\bar r(t_1)+(t-t_1)v_+$ for all $t\ge t_1$;
   symmetrically for the incoming branch with $v_-$. The perpendicular
   distance from the force centre of the incoming line and of the outgoing
   line is the same number
   $$b=\frac{J}{\mu v_\infty}=\frac{J}{\sqrt{2\mu E}},\qquad\text{so that}\qquad J=\mu b\,v_\infty .$$
3. **(Polar advance and deflection.)** Let $(\rho,\theta)$ be polar data of
   $r$ in an oriented orthonormal triad with $e_3=j/J$
   ([[thm-cm-central-force-polar-reduction]]). Then
   $$\Delta:=\theta(+\infty)-\theta(t_*)=\theta(t_*)-\theta(-\infty) =\int_{r_*}^{\infty}\frac{J\,\mathrm dr}{r^2\sqrt{2\mu\,\bigl(E-V(r)\bigr)}}$$
   is finite and positive, and the asymptotic directions satisfy
   $$\frac{v_+}{|v_+|}=-R_{2\Delta}\Bigl(\frac{v_-}{|v_-|}\Bigr),\qquad \frac{\langle v_-,v_+\rangle}{|v_-|\,|v_+|}=\cos(\pi-2\Delta),$$
   where $R_\alpha$ is the rotation of the plane
   $\operatorname{span}(e_1,e_2)$ by $\alpha$. The scattering angle of the
   motion is $\theta_{\mathrm s}=\arccos(\cos(\pi-2\Delta))$; if
   $0<\Delta<\pi/2$ then $\theta_{\mathrm s}=\pi-2\Delta\in(0,\pi)$ and the
   signed velocity rotation is $2\Delta-\pi$.
4. **(Cross-section of a deflection branch.)** Let
   $\theta:(a_1,a_2)\to(0,\pi)$ be a deflection branch of the model in the
   sense of [[def-cm15-cross-section]]: $\theta$ is $C^1$ with
   $\theta'(b)\ne0$, and for every $b\in(a_1,a_2)$ the scattering motion of
   the model with impact parameter $b$, energy $E$ and angular momentum
   $Je_3$ has scattering angle $\theta_{\mathrm s}(b)=\theta(b)$, with
   $0<\Delta(b)<\pi/2$. Then, for every continuous
   $2\pi$-periodic $g:(0,\pi)\times\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$,
   $$\int_{a_1}^{a_2}\!\!\int_0^{2\pi} g\bigl(\theta(b),\varphi\bigr)\;b\;\mathrm db\,\mathrm d\varphi =\int_{\theta_1}^{\theta_2}\!\!\int_0^{2\pi} g(\theta,\varphi)\;b(\theta)\,\bigl|b'(\theta)\bigr|\;\mathrm d\theta\,\mathrm d\varphi,$$
   the outgoing angular measure of the branch has density
   $b(\theta)|b'(\theta)|$ with respect to $\mathrm d\theta\,\mathrm d\varphi$,
   and the differential cross-section of the branch is
   $$\frac{\mathrm d\sigma}{\mathrm d\Omega}(\theta) =\frac{b(\theta)\,\bigl|b'(\theta)\bigr|}{\sin\theta} =\frac{b(\theta)}{\sin\theta\,\bigl|\theta'(b(\theta))\bigr|}\qquad(\theta_1<\theta<\theta_2).$$
   Under the uniform-incident preparation of
   [[def-cm15-asymptotic-data]] clause (iv) with cutoff
   $b_{\max}\in(a_1,a_2]$ and flux $\Phi$, the model predicts the expected
   scattered rate
   $$\dot N=\Phi\,\sigma\bigl((\theta(a_1),\theta(b_{\max}))\bigr),\qquad \sigma(Y)=\int_Y\frac{\mathrm d\sigma}{\mathrm d\Omega}(\theta)\,2\pi\sin\theta\,\mathrm d\theta,$$
   into the corresponding window of scattering angles.
5. **(Scope of the statement.)** The theorem asserts nothing about the
   deflection map outside the recorded branch: it neither asserts that
   $b\mapsto\theta_{\mathrm s}$ is decreasing, injective or free of
   stationary points, nor that the branch images cover $(0,\pi)$; and it
   treats finite-range potentials only. The collisions, long-range
   potentials, velocity-dependent forces and external forces are excluded by
   the model class of [[post-cm05-central-model]] and by (H1).

For $b>a$ the line misses the shell; at $b=a$ it has the adopted free grazing continuation. In both cases the deflection is $0$.

Monotonicity: differentiating [L3], $$\theta'(b)=2\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{a^2-b^2}}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{n^2a^2-b^2}}\right)>0\qquad(0<b<a),$$ because $n>1$ gives $\sqrt{n^2a^2-b^2}>\sqrt{a^2-b^2}>0$, so the first reciprocal exceeds the second; hence $\theta$ is strictly increasing on $(0,a)$, the opposite of the claimed decrease.

Consistency of the contact rule: at the entry the angular momentum about the centre is $\mu b v_\infty$, and inside it equals $\mu a v_{\mathrm{in}}\sin\beta=\mu a\,nv_\infty\sin\beta=\mu b v_\infty$, so angular momentum is conserved across the interface as the radial contact force requires; the energy is conserved by construction of $v_{\mathrm{in}}$ with $U_0=\frac54E$. This separate contact model is conservative and finite-range as an adopted radial rule; it is not a member of the smooth central-scattering class.

Values and the grazing jump: $\theta(0)=0$ and, as $b\uparrow a$, $\alpha\to\pi/2$ and $\beta\to\arcsin(1/n)=\arcsin\frac23$, so $\theta(b)\to\pi-2\arcsin\frac23\approx1.682$ rad $\approx96.4^\circ$; while for every $b\ge a$ the deflection is $0$. The map is therefore not decreasing (it increases on $(0,a)$ and then drops to $0$), and it is not injective: the value $0$ is attained for every $b\ge a$, in addition to its branch value at $b=0$.

Conclusion: step 1.3 refutes the stated global strict-decrease claim with a genuine smooth central-scattering model satisfying its positive-energy, nonzero-angular-momentum and unique-angle hypotheses. More generally, any finite-range model whose angle is defined for every positive impact parameter has the constant free tail established there, so global strict decrease fails even when the interaction inside the range is nontrivial. Steps 1.1-3.1 separately retain the increasing refracting-shell branch and its adopted grazing jump; that contact comparison lies outside the smooth class and supplies no claim that $C^2$ regularity implies or is necessary for monotonicity. The central-scattering theorem itself records no global monotonicity claim and assumes a chosen nondegenerate branch for its cross-section formula.

Genuine smooth finite-range witness and the general obstruction: fix an adopted smooth central model on time window $\mathbb R$ with $u(r)=0$ for $r\ge R$, and let $b>R$, $v_\infty=\sqrt{2E/\mu}$ and $r_b(t)=(v_\infty t,b,0)$. Then $|r_b(t)|\ge b>R$, so $u=u'=0$ along it and $r_b''=0$ solves the reduced equation. With $M=m_1+m_2$, the curves $x_1=(m_2/M)r_b$, $x_2=-(m_1/M)r_b$ have separation $r_b$, zero accelerations and zero force, hence are motions of the adopted model with zero centre of mass. Their angular momentum has magnitude $J=\mu b v_\infty>0$ and energy $E$; at the turning radius $b$, $V(b)=E$, $V'(b)=-J^2/(\mu b^3)<0$ and $V(r)<E$ for every $r>b$, matching [L4]. Both asymptotic relative velocities equal $(v_\infty,0,0)$, so the deflection is uniquely $0$. Any incoming line with impact parameter $b>R$ stays outside the interaction region and continues freely; thus every finite-range model has this constant deflection tail. In particular $u=0$ is $C^2$ and finite-range, and the same construction works for every $b>0$, giving a unique angle $0$ for every positive impact parameter; two distinct positive parameters therefore violate the asserted strict decrease.

citations.quote: 1. **(Momentum continuity.)** The total momentum is continuous across the impact, $$P(t_*^+)=P(t_*^-),\qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad \sum_{i=1}^2 m_i\bigl(v_i^+-v_i^-\bigr)=0,$$ and the impulse delivered to label $1$ is removed from label $2$: $J=m_1(v_1^+-v_1^-)=-m_2(v_2^+-v_2^-)$. 2. **(Smooth-force exclusion.)** Let $x$ be a motion of the smooth force branch of [[post-cm02-force-superposition]] and [[def-cm02-newtonian-flow]] on $I$ along which the force maps are continuous. Then the momentum curves $p_i=m_ix_i'$ are of class $C^1$ on $I$; in particular $$p_i(t_*^+)=p_i(t_*^-)\qquad(i=1,2),$$ so $J=0$: no motion of that class carries a nonzero isolated impulse. The finite-jump model of [[post-cm15-impulse]] clause (i) is therefore a genuine extension of the smooth-force branch, not one of its cases. 3. **(Collinear restitution solution.)** Suppose in addition that the contact is collinear with contact direction $n$ and coefficient of restitution $e\in[0,1]$ ([[post-cm15-impulse]] clause (ii)). Then $$J=\mu(1+e)\bigl(v_2^--v_1^-\bigr),$$ $J$ is parallel to $n$, the centre-of-mass velocity $V:=M^{-1}(m_1v_1^-+m_2v_2^-)$ is unchanged across the impact, and the post-impact velocities are $$v_1^+=V+\frac{m_2}{M}\,e\,\bigl(v_2^--v_1^-\bigr),\qquad v_2^+=V-\frac{m_1}{M}\,e\,\bigl(v_2^--v_1^-\bigr).$$ 4. **(Kinetic energy of the impact.)** The kinetic-energy change across the impact is $$\Delta K:=\frac{m_1\lVert v_1^+\rVert_2^2+m_2\lVert v_2^+\rVert_2^2}{2} -\frac{m_1\lVert v_1^-\rVert_2^2+m_2\lVert v_2^-\rVert_2^2}{2} =-\frac{1-e^2}{2}\,\mu\,\lVert v_2^--v_1^-\rVert_2^2\le0,$$ with equality if and only if $e=1$ or $v_2^-=v_1^-$. For $0\le e<1$ the contact model is dissipative: the total kinetic energy of the two labels is not conserved across the impact, and the deficit $\frac{1-e^2}{2}\mu\lVert v_2^--v_1^-\rVert_2^2$ is a quantity of the adopted contact law.

**a.** $m_1(v_1^+-v_1^-)=J$ and $m_2(v_2^+-v_2^-)=-J$; consequently the total momentum is continuous across the impulse, $p_1(t_*^+)+p_2(t_*^+)=p_1(t_*^-)+p_2(t_*^-)$. **b.** Let $e\in[0,1]$ satisfy the **restitution law** $v_2^+-v_1^+=-e(v_2^--v_1^-)$. Then the post-impulse velocities are uniquely determined: with $V:=\frac{m_1v_1^-+m_2v_2^-}{M}=\frac{m_1v_1^++m_2v_2^+}{M}$, $$v_1^+=V+\frac{m_2}{M}e\,(v_2^--v_1^-),\qquad v_2^+=V-\frac{m_1}{M}e\,(v_2^--v_1^-).$$ **c.** The kinetic-energy change across the impulse is $$\Delta K:=\frac{m_1\lVert v_1^+\rVert_2^2+m_2\lVert v_2^+\rVert_2^2}{2}-\frac{m_1\lVert v_1^-\rVert_2^2+m_2\lVert v_2^-\rVert_2^2}{2}=-\frac{1-e^2}{2}\,\mu\,\lVert v_2^--v_1^-\rVert_2^2\le0;$$ in particular $\Delta K=0$ for $e=1$ and $\Delta K=-\frac12\mu\lVert v_2^--v_1^-\rVert_2^2$ for $e=0$.

Let $N\ge1$, let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval with at least two points ([[def-interval]]), let $m_1,\dots,m_N>0$ and let $x_i:I\to\mathbb R^3$ be differentiable at every point of $I$ ([[def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral]]). Put $M:=\sum_{i}m_i>0$, $X:=M^{-1}\sum_{i}m_ix_i$ and $\rho_i:=x_i-X$; all sums over $i$ range over $1,\dots,N$ (the index set $\{1,\dots,N\}$ of [[lem-finite-sum-laws]]), and $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$, $\lVert\cdot\rVert_2$ are the Euclidean inner product and norm on $\mathbb R^3$ ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]]). Then: 1. $X$ and every $\rho_i$ are differentiable on $I$, with $X'=M^{-1}\sum_im_ix_i'$ and $\rho_i'=x_i'-X'$, and the identities $\sum_im_i\rho_i=0$ and $\sum_im_i\rho_i'=0$ hold on $I$; 2. for every $t\in I$, $$\sum_{i}m_i\lVert x_i'(t)\rVert_2^2=M\lVert X'(t)\rVert_2^2+\sum_{i}m_i\lVert\rho_i'(t)\rVert_2^2;$$ 3. if $N=2$, then with $r:=x_1-x_2$ and $\mu:=m_1m_2/M$ one has $\sum_im_i\lVert\rho_i'(t)\rVert_2^2=\mu\lVert r'(t)\rVert_2^2$ and hence $$\sum_{i}m_i\lVert x_i'(t)\rVert_2^2=M\lVert X'(t)\rVert_2^2+\mu\lVert r'(t)\rVert_2^2$$ for every $t\in I$.

**(b) Total mass, total momentum, centre of mass, relative positions.** Define $$M:=\sum_{i}m_{i}>0,\qquad p_{i}:=m_{i}w_{i},\qquad P(t):=\sum_{i}p_{i}(t),\qquad X(t):=M^{-1}\sum_{i}m_{i}x_{i}(t),\qquad \rho_{i}:=x_{i}-X.$$ Here $p_{i}$ is the **momentum** of label $i$, $P$ the **total momentum**, $X$ the **centre of mass** and $\rho_{i}$ the **relative position** of label $i$. The dimensions are $[M]=\mu$, $[p_{i}]=[P]=\mu\ell\tau^{-1}$ (read in $\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$) and $[X]=[\rho_{i}]=\ell$ ([[def-cm01-units]]).

The **Euclidean inner product** of $x, y \in \mathbb{R}^{n}$ is the real number $$\langle x, y\rangle \;:=\; \sum_{k<n} x_k\,y_k ,$$ the finite sum of [[def-finite-sum]] applied to the list $k \mapsto x_k y_k$ (extended by $0$ beyond $n$, as every finite list in this library is). The **Euclidean norm** of $x$ is $$\lVert x\rVert_2 \;:=\; \sqrt{\langle x, x\rangle},$$ which is defined because $\langle x,x\rangle = \sum_{k<n} x_k^{2} \ge 0$ (a sum of nonnegative terms, [[lem-finite-sum-laws]] clause 4 and [[lem-of-square-positive]], the case $x_k = 0$ giving $x_k^2 = 0$ by [[def-integer-power]]) and every nonnegative real has a unique nonnegative square root ([[thm-of-square-roots]]).

**(i) The two-label central model.** A model of class (i) is a force model of [[post-cm02-force-superposition]] with $N=2$ labels, fixed masses $m_1,m_2>0$ ([[post-cm01-worldlines]] clause (v)), a time window $I_0$, the collision-excluded configuration domain $$Q:=\{\,x=(x_1,x_2)\in(\mathbb R^3)^2:\lvert x_1-x_2\rvert\in J_0\,\}$$ for an open interval $J_0\subseteq(0,\infty)$ ([[def-cm01-configuration]]), and the force map presented through the time-independent **static central pair potential** $$U(x_1,x_2):=u(\lvert x_1-x_2\rvert),\qquad u:J_0\to\mathbb R\ \text{of class }C^2,$$ so that $F_i(t,x,v)=-\nabla_{x_i}U(x)$ on the state domain (clauses (iii) and (iv) of [[post-cm02-interactions]]; $U$ is of class $C^2$ on the open $Q$ by [[lem-cm05-radial-potential-gradient]]). In the external-plus-pair presentation of clause (i) of that postulate the model has $F_i^{\mathrm{ext}}\equiv0$: no external forces act on the labels of a model of class (i).

**(d) Dimensions of the quantities of this framework.** The dimension map is fixed on the following quantities: 1. coordinates: $[t]=\tau$ and $[x_{i}]=\ell$; 2. velocity components: $[w_{i}]=\ell\tau^{-1}$; 3. acceleration components: $[a_{i}]=\ell\tau^{-2}$; 4. mass: $[m]=\mu$, and the mass operator (multiplication of spatial components by masses) has dimension $\mu$; 5. angles and entries of rotation matrices: dimensionless, $[R_{ij}]=1$ for $R\in SO(3)$ under the radian convention, in which an angle is the ratio of an arc length to a radius and therefore a ratio of two lengths; 6. the standard derived quantities have the dimensions obtained from the rules of (b) once their defining relations are stated: momentum $\mu\ell\tau^{-1}$, force $\mu\ell\tau^{-2}$, energy $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$, action $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-1}$, angular momentum $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-1}$;

The **intervals** of $\mathbb{R}$ are the sets of the following nine forms, where $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$: | | bounded forms | | one-sided and full forms | |---|---|---|---| | $(a,b)$ | $\{x : a < x < b\}$ | $(a,\infty)$ | $\{x : a < x\}$ | | $[a,b]$ | $\{x : a \le x \le b\}$ | $[a,\infty)$ | $\{x : a \le x\}$ | | $[a,b)$ | $\{x : a \le x < b\}$ | $(-\infty,b)$ | $\{x : x < b\}$ | | $(a,b]$ | $\{x : a < x \le b\}$ | $(-\infty,b]$ | $\{x : x \le b\}$ | | | | $(-\infty,\infty)$ | $\mathbb{R}$ | An interval is **open** when both of its written endpoints are excluded, that is for the forms $(a,b)$, $(a,\infty)$, $(-\infty,b)$ and $(-\infty,\infty)$; it is **closed** when both written endpoints are included, that is for $[a,b]$, $[a,\infty)$, $(-\infty,b]$ and $(-\infty,\infty)$.

derivations.claim: Data: $M=2$, $\mu=\frac12$, $V=\frac{1\cdot1+1\cdot(-1)}{2}=0$, $d^-=-2n$, so $\lVert d^-\rVert_2^2=4$ and the incoming kinetic energy is $K^-=\frac12(1)+\frac12(1)=1\ \mathrm{J}$.

Impact outcome: the restitution law gives $v_2^+-v_1^+=-2\,d^-=+4n$, and [L1] gives $v_1^+=V+\frac{m_2}{M}e\,d^-=0+\frac12\cdot2\cdot(-2)n=-2n$, $v_2^+=V-\frac{m_1}{M}e\,d^-=+2n$. The total momentum is $(-2)+(+2)=0$, continuous across the impact, so the momentum account of the model is satisfied.

Energy: the post-impact kinetic energy is $K^+=\frac12(4)+\frac12(4)=4\ \mathrm{J}$, so $\Delta K=+3\ \mathrm{J}$, in agreement with the formula $\Delta K=-\frac{1-e^2}{2}\mu\lVert d^-\rVert_2^2=-\frac{1-4}{2}\cdot\frac12\cdot4=+3\ \mathrm{J}$.

Potential energy: by [L2] the configuration, hence $U$, is unchanged across the instant of the impact: $U(t_*^+)=U(t_*^-)$. Therefore the total mechanical energy jumps by $\Delta(K+U)=\Delta K=+3\ \mathrm{J}>0$ across the impact.

Failure of the false statement: along a motion that is conservative away from the impact (constant $K+U$ on each of $I\cap(-\infty,t_*)$ and $I\cap(t_*,+\infty)$), the total mechanical energy cannot increase across the impact; the witness with $e=2$ and $d^-\ne0$ does increase it, so the asserted universal admissibility of real $e$ fails. Equivalently, a rule with $e>1$ requires an internal energy reservoir that is released during the contact (as the cited engineering source describes for superelastic collisions): the two-label mechanical account is then incomplete, and such a rule is not a conservative contact law of the restricted model.

Restriction: for $0\le e\le1$ the same formula gives $\Delta K=-\frac{1-e^2}{2}\mu\lVert d^-\rVert_2^2\le0$, with equality exactly at $e=1$ (or $d^-=0$); hence within the page's model the conservative case is $e=1$ and the dissipative contact laws are $0\le e<1$, exactly the restriction adopted in [[post-cm15-impulse]] clause (ii).

citations.quote: **(i) The isolated reciprocal impulse model.** A two-label force model with masses $m_1,m_2>0$ ([[post-cm01-worldlines]] clause (v)), time window $I_0$, configuration domain $Q$ ([[def-cm01-configuration]]) and continuous external-plus-pair force maps $F_1,F_2$ is **run in the isolated reciprocal impulse model at $t_*\in I_0$** when there is a motion $x=(x_1,x_2):I\to Q$ of the associated first-order system ([[def-cm02-newtonian-flow]]) such that: 1. $x_1,x_2$ are continuous on $I$ and twice continuously differentiable on each of $I\cap(-\infty,t_*)$ and $I\cap(t_*,\infty)$ ([[def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral]], [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]), and $m_ix_i''(t)=F_i(t,x(t),x'(t))$ for every $t\in I\setminus\{t_*\}$; 2. the one-sided limits $v_i^{\pm}:=\lim_{t\to t_*\pm}x_i'(t)$ exist in $\mathbb R^3$ ([[def-vector-valued-functions-limits-and-continuity]]); 3. there is a vector $J\in\mathbb R^3$, the **impulse**, with $$m_1\bigl(v_1^+-v_1^-\bigr)=J,\qquad m_2\bigl(v_2^+-v_2^-\bigr)=-J .$$ The two equations of clause 3 are the **reciprocal finite-jump form** of the isolated impulse: the two labels receive equal and opposite momentum changes. The model places no bound on the force maps across $t_*$; its distributional rendering by test-function pairings is proved in [[thm-cm-impulse-restitution-and-energy-loss]]. The dimension of the impulse is $[J]=\mathsf M\ell\tau^{-1}$ ([[def-cm01-units]]).

1. **(Momentum continuity.)** The total momentum is continuous across the impact, $$P(t_*^+)=P(t_*^-),\qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad \sum_{i=1}^2 m_i\bigl(v_i^+-v_i^-\bigr)=0,$$ and the impulse delivered to label $1$ is removed from label $2$: $J=m_1(v_1^+-v_1^-)=-m_2(v_2^+-v_2^-)$.

Let $N\ge1$, let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval with at least two points ([[def-interval]]), let $m_1,\dots,m_N>0$ and let $x_i:I\to\mathbb R^3$ be differentiable at every point of $I$ ([[def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral]]). Put $M:=\sum_{i}m_i>0$, $X:=M^{-1}\sum_{i}m_ix_i$ and $\rho_i:=x_i-X$; all sums over $i$ range over $1,\dots,N$ (the index set $\{1,\dots,N\}$ of [[lem-finite-sum-laws]]), and $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$, $\lVert\cdot\rVert_2$ are the Euclidean inner product and norm on $\mathbb R^3$ ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]]). Then: 1. $X$ and every $\rho_i$ are differentiable on $I$, with $X'=M^{-1}\sum_im_ix_i'$ and $\rho_i'=x_i'-X'$, and the identities $\sum_im_i\rho_i=0$ and $\sum_im_i\rho_i'=0$ hold on $I$; 2. for every $t\in I$, $$\sum_{i}m_i\lVert x_i'(t)\rVert_2^2=M\lVert X'(t)\rVert_2^2+\sum_{i}m_i\lVert\rho_i'(t)\rVert_2^2;$$ 3. if $N=2$, then with $r:=x_1-x_2$ and $\mu:=m_1m_2/M$ one has $\sum_im_i\lVert\rho_i'(t)\rVert_2^2=\mu\lVert r'(t)\rVert_2^2$ and hence $$\sum_{i}m_i\lVert x_i'(t)\rVert_2^2=M\lVert X'(t)\rVert_2^2+\mu\lVert r'(t)\rVert_2^2$$ for every $t\in I$.

**(b) Total mass, total momentum, centre of mass, relative positions.** Define $$M:=\sum_{i}m_{i}>0,\qquad p_{i}:=m_{i}w_{i},\qquad P(t):=\sum_{i}p_{i}(t),\qquad X(t):=M^{-1}\sum_{i}m_{i}x_{i}(t),\qquad \rho_{i}:=x_{i}-X.$$ Here $p_{i}$ is the **momentum** of label $i$, $P$ the **total momentum**, $X$ the **centre of mass** and $\rho_{i}$ the **relative position** of label $i$. The dimensions are $[M]=\mu$, $[p_{i}]=[P]=\mu\ell\tau^{-1}$ (read in $\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$) and $[X]=[\rho_{i}]=\ell$ ([[def-cm01-units]]).

The **Euclidean inner product** of $x, y \in \mathbb{R}^{n}$ is the real number $$\langle x, y\rangle \;:=\; \sum_{k<n} x_k\,y_k ,$$ the finite sum of [[def-finite-sum]] applied to the list $k \mapsto x_k y_k$ (extended by $0$ beyond $n$, as every finite list in this library is). The **Euclidean norm** of $x$ is $$\lVert x\rVert_2 \;:=\; \sqrt{\langle x, x\rangle},$$ which is defined because $\langle x,x\rangle = \sum_{k<n} x_k^{2} \ge 0$ (a sum of nonnegative terms, [[lem-finite-sum-laws]] clause 4 and [[lem-of-square-positive]], the case $x_k = 0$ giving $x_k^2 = 0$ by [[def-integer-power]]) and every nonnegative real has a unique nonnegative square root ([[thm-of-square-roots]]).

derivations.claim: Common data: $M=8$, $\mu=\frac32$, $V=\frac{2\cdot3+6\cdot(-1)}{8}=0$, $d^-=-4n$, $\lVert d^-\rVert_2^2=16$, $K^-=12\ \mathrm{J}$.
Outcome (a), sticking: $v_1^+=v_2^+=0$. Then $m_1(v_1^+-v_1^-)=2(0-3)n=-6n$ and $m_2(v_2^+-v_2^-)=6(0+1)n=+6n$; the impulse is $J=-6n\ \mathrm{N\,s}$ and the total momentum is $0=P^-$.
Outcome (b), elastic: $v_1^+=-3n$, $v_2^+=+1n$. Then $m_1(v_1^+-v_1^-)=2(-6)n=-12n$ and $m_2(v_2^+-v_2^-)=6(+2)n=+12n$; the impulse is $J=-12n\ \mathrm{N\,s}$ and the total momentum is $0=P^-$.

Both outcomes satisfy the reciprocal impulse equations of [L1], with different impulses ($-6n$ versus $-12n$), and the same given incoming data; their post-impact velocities differ ($0$ versus $-3n$ and $+1n$). Hence the impulse equations alone do not fix the post-impact velocities, and the false statement fails.

Energy: by [L2] the changes are $\Delta K_{(a)}=\frac32\cdot\frac12(0-16)=-12\ \mathrm{J}$ and $\Delta K_{(b)}=\frac32\cdot\frac12(16-16)=0$; the outcomes are therefore also distinguished by their energy accounting, so no choice of impulse can be recovered from the momentum data and the two outcomes are genuinely different model histories.

Consequence: in the collinear isolated-impact model the contact law of [[post-cm15-impulse]] clause (ii) (equivalently, the coefficient $e$, or a dynamical contact model producing the impulse) is an independent model datum; the reciprocal impulse equations constrain only the *sum* $m_1\Delta v_1+m_2\Delta v_2=0$. The same conclusion is recorded as clause 5 of [[pthm-cm15-impact-balance]].
